fat-intake-calculator.assumptionNote: Macro targets are starting points, not medical advice. People with heart disease, diabetes or lipid disorders should get personalised targets from a clinician.
benefits: Turns 'eat less fat' into an exact daily gram target you can track.
Shows the healthy 20-35% range and the saturated-fat cap in one view.
Helps you read food labels with context: grams per serving versus your cap.
Pairs with the carb calculator to complete your macro picture.

faqs.a: Fat carries vitamins A, D, E and K, cushions organs, builds cell membranes and hormones, and makes food satisfying. Diets with almost no fat often backfire.
faqs.q: Why does the body need fat?

faqs.a: Unsaturated fats (olive oil, nuts, fish) support heart health. Saturated fats (butter, fatty meat, coconut oil) should stay under 10% of calories. Trans fats should be avoided almost entirely.
Guidelines say under 10% of calories from saturated fat, which is about 24 g on a 2,200 kcal diet. Lower is generally better for blood cholesterol.
faqs.q: How much saturated fat is too much?

faqs.a: Fat slows digestion, so meals with healthy fat keep you full longer and steady blood sugar. Very low-fat meals often lead to rebound snacking.
One tablespoon of oil is about 14 g of fat, a handful of almonds about 14 g, one egg about 5 g, and a cup of whole milk about 8 g. Cooking oil is the stealthiest source.
faqs.q: How much fat is in common foods?

faqs.a: Not directly. Excess calories from any macro store as body fat. Fat is simply the most calorie-dense macro at 9 kcal per gram, so portions matter more.
faqs.q: Does eating fat make you fat?

fat-intake-calculator.formula:
Fat grams = daily calories x fat % / 100 / 9.
Fat provides 9 kcal per gram.
AMDR healthy range: 20-35% of calories. Saturated fat cap: under 10% of calories.
howTo: Enter your daily calorie target (use the TDEE calculator if you do not know it).
Pick your fat mix: balanced, low-fat or higher-fat.
Read your daily fat target in grams, the healthy 20-35% range and the saturated-fat cap.
Compare food labels against your target when planning meals.
keyFacts: Fat provides 9 kcal per gram, more than double carbs or protein.
The accepted healthy range (AMDR) is 20-35% of daily calories from fat.
Saturated fat should stay under 10% of calories for heart health.
Unsaturated fats from nuts, olive oil and fish are the healthiest choices.
Trans fats should be avoided as much as possible.
A 2,200 kcal balanced diet at 25% fat means about 61 g of fat per day.

fat-intake-calculator.quickAnswer: Daily fat comes from your calories times your fat share, divided by 9 kcal per gram. On a 2,200 kcal balanced diet at 25% fat, the target is about 61 g per day, inside the healthy range of 49-86 g. Saturated fat should stay under 10% of calories, about 24 g here.
fat-intake-calculator.tagline: Find your daily fat target in grams - balanced, low-fat or higher-fat, with the saturated cap.
fat-intake-calculator.workedExample:
2,200 kcal, balanced mix (25%):
1. Calories from fat = 2,200 x 25 / 100 = 550 kcal.
2. Grams = 550 / 9 = 61.1 g/day.
3. Healthy range: 2,200 x 20% / 9 = 48.9 g up to 2,200 x 35% / 9 = 85.6 g.
4. Saturated cap: 2,200 x 10% / 9 = 24.4 g/day maximum.
